mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months indicates economic weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained increases in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a weakening supply side, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% within the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals increased consumer spending, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained increases in GDPC1.
